CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. To improvise a rhythmic pattern means to (1 mark)
   A. stay silent
   B. copy it from a book only
   C. make it up on the spot
   D. write it before playing

2. Which twigs are best for making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Green leaves
   B. Thick logs
   C. Dry, straight twigs about as thick as a pencil
   D. Wet, bent branches

3. Who stops the game with a whistle for a rule break? (1 mark)
   A. The shooter
   B. The spectator
   C. The umpire
   D. The goal keeper

4. What does giving with the ball mean? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing the ball away
   B. Kicking the ball
   C. Handing the ball to the umpire
   D. Bending the arms as the ball arrives to soften the catch

5. A chest pass starts with the ball held at (1 mark)
   A. the ankles
   B. behind the back
   C. above the head
   D. chest height

6. Which of these letters has neither an ascender nor a descender? (1 mark)
   A. p
   B. d
   C. b
   D. a

7. Which letter has an ascender? (1 mark)
   A. e
   B. o
   C. b
   D. a

8. How many guide lines are used for practising lettering in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Two
   C. Six
   D. Ten

9. Which move skips over a note? (1 mark)
   A. d to m
   B. m to r
   C. r to m
   D. d to r

10. Variation in a melody means using (1 mark)
   A. only one syllable
   B. different syllables and note lengths
   C. only rests
   D. no rhythm

11. Which nationality was Zoltan Kodaly, whose method uses hand signs? (1 mark)
   A. Hungarian
   B. Brazilian
   C. Kenyan
   D. Chinese

12. Which melody uses only steps? (1 mark)
   A. d m d m
   B. d r m r d
   C. d d m d
   D. m d m d

13. In a medium start, the rear knee is level with (1 mark)
   A. the start line
   B. the toe of the back foot
   C. the middle of the front foot
   D. the heel of the front foot

14. A sprint is (1 mark)
   A. a throwing event
   B. a very long race
   C. a short race run at full speed
   D. a jump into sand

15. Which is a safety rule for sprint races? (1 mark)
   A. Push to get ahead
   B. Never push or trip another runner
   C. Run in any lane
   D. Run backwards

16. A sequence in gymnastics is (1 mark)
   A. a set of movements performed in a fixed order
   B. a type of mat
   C. a single balance
   D. a rule break

17. The message of a song is (1 mark)
   A. the number of singers
   B. the name of the drum
   C. the main idea the singers want us to hear
   D. the colour of the stage

18. Dynamics means (1 mark)
   A. the words
   B. the speed
   C. the pitch
   D. how loud or soft the music is

19. Which is good singing posture? (1 mark)
   A. Slouching
   B. Hiding behind others
   C. Standing tall with shoulders relaxed
   D. Bending over

20. The element of light means (1 mark)
   A. the price
   B. how well the subject is lit
   C. the weight of the camera
   D. the size of the photo

21. Which is used only for taking photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Torch
   B. Radio
   C. Whistle
   D. Digital camera

22. Which note is played with the thumb hole and hole 1 covered? (1 mark)
   A. B
   B. A
   C. C
   D. G

23. When should you swim? (1 mark)
   A. In the dark
   B. Only when a teacher or lifeguard is watching
   C. Alone
   D. Whenever you like

24. How should you use steps or a ladder to enter? (1 mark)
   A. Jump onto them
   B. Ignore rails
   C. Go head first
   D. Face the steps, hold the rails and go feet first

25. Animal games are inspired by (1 mark)
   A. the movements and behaviour of animals
   B. tall buildings
   C. clouds
   D. cars

26. The elephant walk is done by (1 mark)
   A. running
   B. crawling
   C. bending forward and letting your arms hang like a trunk
   D. jumping high

27. Counting steps and jumps in animal games links to (1 mark)
   A. Geography maps
   B. Chemistry
   C. Foreign languages only
   D. Mathematics

28. When the anthem is sung, you should (1 mark)
   A. stand straight and be quiet
   B. run
   C. play
   D. sit and talk

29. Aesthetic refers to (1 mark)
   A. how long it is
   B. how beautiful or pleasing something is
   C. how heavy it is
   D. how cheap it is

30. Which value is found in the Kenya National Anthem? (1 mark)
   A. Laziness
   B. Selfishness
   C. Unity
   D. Cheating

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write rhythm patterns for the elephant walk and the hare hop using rhythm names. (3 marks)

32. State the recorder notes that match d, r and m. (3 marks)

33. Describe how to compose, write and perform an original four-beat rhythmic pattern. (5 marks)

34. What are indigenous games? (2 marks)

35. Identify the kayamba and the drum by giving the name, the community or area and the way of playing for each. (4 marks)

36. Give three common mistakes in the crab balance and how to fix them. (3 marks)

37. State three mistakes in gliding and how to correct them. (3 marks)

38. Explain how good singing performance is achieved, using posture, breathing, diction, expression and etiquette. (5 marks)

39. Why do we get up slowly after a side roll? (3 marks)

40. Describe how to make a chest pass. (4 marks)

41. Explain what tone or value means in a drawing. (3 marks)

42. Explain what a relay race is and how it teaches teamwork. (4 marks)

43. State what red, white and the shield stand for on the Kenyan flag. (3 marks)

44. Give three reasons for flying the Kenyan flag at an athletics event. (3 marks)

45. Explain why netball is called a team game. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — make it up on the spot
   Improvising is inventing a pattern without preparing it first.

2. C — Dry, straight twigs about as thick as a pencil
   Dry, straight, thin twigs burn evenly into good drawing sticks.

3. C — The umpire
   Umpires control the game and blow the whistle.

4. D — Bending the arms as the ball arrives to soften the catch
   Bending the arms takes the force out of the ball.

5. D — chest height
   A chest pass begins with the ball at chest level.

6. D — a
   The letter a sits between the baseline and the top of small letters.

7. C — b
   The stem of b goes up above the small letters.

8. A — Four
   Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line make four.

9. A — d to m
   Going from d to m skips r.

10. B — different syllables and note lengths
   Variation makes a tune interesting.

11. A — Hungarian
   Zoltan Kodaly was a Hungarian music teacher.

12. B — d r m r d
   Each move in d r m r d is to a neighbouring note.

13. C — the middle of the front foot
   The medium start places the rear knee by the middle of the front foot.

14. C — a short race run at full speed
   Sprints such as 50 m or 100 m are short races.

15. B — Never push or trip another runner
   Pushing or tripping can hurt people.

16. A — a set of movements performed in a fixed order
   A sequence links skills one after the other.

17. C — the main idea the singers want us to hear
   Message is the main idea.

18. D — how loud or soft the music is
   Dynamics are the loud and soft parts.

19. C — Standing tall with shoulders relaxed
   Good posture helps breathing.

20. B — how well the subject is lit
   Light is a key element.

21. D — Digital camera
   A digital camera is made for photography.

22. A — B
   B uses the thumb and the first hole.

23. B — Only when a teacher or lifeguard is watching
   Supervision keeps swimmers safe.

24. D — Face the steps, hold the rails and go feet first
   Use the rails and enter carefully.

25. A — the movements and behaviour of animals
   Children copy how animals move.

26. C — bending forward and letting your arms hang like a trunk
   Slow heavy steps with arms as a trunk.

27. D — Mathematics
   Counting is a maths skill.

28. A — stand straight and be quiet
   Show respect.

29. B — how beautiful or pleasing something is
   Aesthetic is about beauty.

30. C — Unity
   The anthem speaks of unity, peace, justice and service.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Elephant walk: taa taa taa (rest). Hare hop: ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pattern, 1 mark for correct rest or names.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: If G is doh, then G, A and B match d, r and m. G is d, A is r and B is m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose four beats. Fill each with a crotchet, a pair of quavers or a rest. Make sure the pattern has variation and ends on a crotchet. Write it with rhythm names and note symbols. Clap it to a steady beat and improve it after feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing beats, using different values, ending on a long note, writing it and performing it.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Traditional games that belong to a people and were passed on from long ago.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Kayamba: coastal people such as the Mijikenda, played by shaking. Drum (ngoma): found in many communities, played with hands or sticks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct name, community or area and method, up to 4.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hips sagging: push harder. Bent arms: straighten them. Head dropped: keep it in line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake with a fix.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lifting the head: keep it between the arms; bent arms or legs: stretch them; pushing too hard: push gently. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Stand tall with a relaxed body. Breathe deeply and sing on the breath. Say the words clearly. Use gestures and facial expressions to show the message and mood. Walk on and off quietly and respect others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five points.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Getting up fast can make you feel dizzy and you may fall. Slowly is safer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dizziness, 1 mark for falling, 1 mark for safety.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold the ball at chest height with both hands. Look at the partner. Step forward and straighten the arms, turning the thumbs down. The ball goes to the partner's chest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tone means how light or dark an area is. In a charcoal drawing, we can make tones from light grey to black by pressing lightly or hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for lightness or darkness, 1 mark for range of tones, 1 mark for charcoal pressure.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: A relay is a race in which each runner in a team runs a short distance and passes a baton to the next runner. The team wins by working together and passing smoothly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for team running, 1 mark for the baton, 2 marks for teamwork explanation.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Red stands for the blood shed for freedom. White stands for peace and honesty. The shield and spears stand for the defence of freedom.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It shows which country the athletes represent; it builds pride and patriotism; it brings people together to cheer; it shows respect to visitors. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Players must pass to each other to move the ball and score. No player can run with the ball alone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for passing or cooperation, 1 mark for the explanation.
